question.problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{0}^{\pi }{e}^{-4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{17}($
{{field-1}} $)$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the indefinite integral by  $I=\int {e}^{-4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that 

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{-4x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4{e}^{-4x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int {e}^{-4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =({e}^{-4x})(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(-4{e}^{-4x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-4\int {e}^{-4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-4J.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we can use integration by parts to evaluate

$$
J=\int {e}^{-4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

To do this, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{-4x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4{e}^{-4x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}J & =\int {e}^{-4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =({e}^{-4x})(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(-4{e}^{-4x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{-4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4I.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into our equation for $I,$ we solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =-{e}^{-4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-4({e}^{-4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4I) \\ I & =-{e}^{-4x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-4{e}^{-4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-16I \\ 17I & =-{e}^{-4x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x+4\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\ I & =-\frac{{e}^{-4x}}{17}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x+4\operatorname{sin}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate our definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{e}^{-4x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =(-\frac{{e}^{-4x}}{17}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x+4\operatorname{sin}⁡x)){|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(-\frac{{e}^{-4\pi }}{17}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )))-(-\frac{1}{17}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)+4\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))) \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-4\pi }}{17}(-1+0)+\frac{1}{17}(1+0) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-4\pi }}{17}+\frac{1}{17} \\  & =\frac{1}{17}(1+{e}^{-4\pi }).\end{aligned}
$$
